analysis.title: Rates Spark: A blue wave in the US and euro inflation
key_insights: A decisive Democratic win in the US midterms supports immediate market sentiment: little risk of the result being challenged, Trump is accepting it, a new Congress takes office in January, and there is no split-Congress gridlock.

Tighter AI regulation is a possible headwind. Data centres were a big midterm topic and Democrats take a firmer stance against the current free-market approach to AI. ING says much of US growth relies on the AI boom, though near-term changes are unlikely.
Trump remains in charge of foreign policy, so inflation is a wild card. The war with Iran is not over and oil barely moved on the election result.
Tariffs could return as a policy tool. ING says another source of inflation uncertainty could push rates higher still, since markets are sensitive to inflation surprises in data.
Implied volatility measures suggest preparing for significant rate moves over the coming months.
Eurozone October flash CPI is seen rising to 4% headline, with core steady at 2.5%. ING says this still points to another ECB rate hike in December.
US ISM services is expected only marginally softer at 54.8. ADP employment is watched ahead of Friday's official jobs data.
Germany auctions 15y and 20y Bunds for a total of €2bn. The US Treasury quarterly refunding announcement is expected to leave coupon issuance unchanged.

sector_views.rationale: Stricter AI and data-centre policy under a Democratic Congress could become a headwind for US growth, which currently leans on the AI boom. Not expected to materialise in big changes in the near term.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Expected rise in headline inflation, consistent with another ECB hike in December.
Expected to remain steady, so the headline rise is not driven by core.
Seen only marginally softer, so services activity is expected to stay firm.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Flash CPI figures still point to a further hike.

tension_points.bull_case: A decisive Democratic win ensures a smooth transition with little risk of the result being challenged, Trump accepting it and no split-Congress gridlock, which supports market sentiment.
tension_points.bear_case: Democrats favour a firmer stance on AI and data centres, and much of US growth relies on the AI boom, so stricter policy could become a headwind and add to AI jitters in equities.
